source: Per-company AR extraction (Screener.in PDFs + IR sites) — Claude.ai routine, daily batch of 20

govt_capex.evidence: ABB India noted in CY2024 results that 'sustained public capex—particularly in infrastructure, railways, and green energy—are driving consumption and demand recovery' and the company 'remains a beneficiary of the government's capex investments in mega infrastructure and renewable projects'. No explicit percentage disclosed.

crude_exposure.evidence: ABB India is an electrical equipment and automation technology manufacturer; primary inputs are metals, electronics, and components. No crude oil/petroleum raw material exposure disclosed.

inr_exposure.evidence: Export revenue is ~10% of total; company uses forward contracts for FX risk management per general ABB India disclosures, but specific USD revenue % and hedging details not accessible from public summaries.

pli_scheme.evidence: No mention of ABB India being a PLI scheme beneficiary in any annual report summary or analyst report reviewed. ABB India's product categories (switchgear, drives, transformers, robots) are not in PLI-covered sectors.

china_plus_one.evidence: Premier Energies reported exports contribute less than 1% of total revenue in FY2025. The company is predominantly a domestic solar cell and module manufacturer supplying the Indian market. No China+1 export narrative identified.

govt_capex.evidence: Premier Energies' customers are primarily large Indian solar project developers and EPCs, many of which execute government-backed renewable energy projects. However, no explicit government capex revenue percentage is disclosed.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Total debt as of March 2025: Rs 1,893 crore. Breakdown between floating and fixed rate not publicly disclosed in summaries reviewed.

crude_exposure.evidence: Key raw materials are solar-grade silicon, wafers, EVA, glass, and backsheet. No meaningful crude oil/petroleum direct raw material exposure. Silver paste is another key input.

inr_exposure.evidence: Exports are less than 1% of revenue in FY2025; USD revenue exposure is negligible. Hedging policy details not available in public summaries.

pli_scheme.evidence: Premier Energies is a PLI scheme beneficiary under the National Programme on High Efficiency Solar PV Modules. The company has commissioned PLI-linked solar cell and module capacity (TOPCon cell facility in Hyderabad commissioned in 2025). Exact PLI incentive amount as % of revenue not disclosed in public summaries.

china_plus_one.evidence: Analyst reports on FY2025 results note Navin Fluorine is 'benefiting from rising preference for Indian fluorochemical suppliers amid China+1 sentiment' and is positioned as 'a key beneficiary of the global supply chain shift toward India.' Company exports to North America, Europe, Middle East, and Asia Pacific. No explicit China+1 revenue attribution found in official AR text.

govt_capex.evidence: Navin Fluorine is a B2B specialty chemicals and CRAMS company; no meaningful government capex exposure.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Specific floating vs fixed rate debt breakdown not available in public summaries of FY2024-25 annual report.

crude_exposure.evidence: Key raw materials are fluorspar, anhydrous hydrofluoric acid (AHF), and specialty organic intermediates. Crude oil/petroleum not a direct primary raw material.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Company enters into foreign exchange forward contracts to hedge export receivables and import payables.
inr_exposure.evidence: ~40% of revenues are export-derived (primarily USD/EUR denominated). Company uses forward contracts for FX risk management per standard disclosures. Specific USD revenue % and hedging ratios not available in public summaries.

pli_scheme.evidence: No PLI scheme beneficiary status found for Navin Fluorine. Specialty fluorochemicals and CRAMS are not covered under India's PLI schemes.

china_plus_one.evidence: NALCO exports aluminium ingots/billets but annual report MD&A does not articulate a China+1 positioning strategy; exports are primarily to Asian and Middle Eastern markets driven by global aluminium demand cycles.

rural.evidence: NALCO is a bulk commodity producer (aluminium, alumina, bauxite); no rural-segment revenue disclosure exists.

govt_capex.evidence: NALCO sells aluminium to downstream fabricators and traders; some indirect linkage to government infrastructure spending but no direct government-capex revenue line disclosed.

rate_sensitive.evidence: NALCO is largely debt-free (net cash positive PSU); minimal borrowings so floating-rate liability percentage is not material.

crude_exposure.evidence: NALCO uses coal (captive mines) and petroleum coke (calcined pet coke for anodes) as key inputs. Pet coke prices track crude oil. Exact % of raw material cost attributable to crude-linked inputs not confirmed without PDF.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: NALCO exports are priced in USD linked to LME aluminium prices. The company uses natural hedges via USD-denominated export revenues offsetting import costs. Limited use of derivative hedges per past disclosures.
inr_exposure.evidence: Approximately 40% of revenues are from exports priced in USD; hedging policy relies primarily on natural hedges.

pli_scheme.evidence: NALCO is a primary aluminium producer (PSU); it is not a beneficiary under any PLI scheme. PLI for specialty steel/advanced chemistry/electronics does not cover commodity aluminium smelting.

china_plus_one.evidence: Syrma SGS positions itself as an India-based EMS alternative benefiting from global supply chain diversification away from China, citing growth in exports and new customer wins from global OEMs. However, explicit China+1 revenue attribution is not separately disclosed in available segments.

govt_capex.evidence: Some exposure via defence electronics and railway electronics segments, but exact government capex-linked revenue % not disclosed without PDF.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Syrma has working capital borrowings that are typically floating rate (linked to MCLR/repo). Exact percentage of total liabilities not confirmed without PDF.

crude_exposure.evidence: Syrma is an electronics manufacturer; primary inputs are PCBs, semiconductors, passive components. Crude oil is not a direct raw material input.

inr_exposure.evidence: Export revenue exists but exact USD revenue % and hedging policy details not confirmed without PDF access.

pli_scheme.evidence: Syrma SGS Technology is an approved beneficiary under PLI Scheme for IT Hardware (PLI 2.0) and has applied/registered under PLI for White Goods. PLI incentive amounts disclosed separately in annual report but exact % of total revenue not confirmed without PDF.

china_plus_one.evidence: Apar Industries has grown its export business significantly in conductors and cables, supplying to US, Middle East, and other markets. Management commentary references global supply chain diversification and export growth momentum, though explicit China+1 attribution without separate revenue line.

rural.evidence: Apar supplies cables and conductors to power utilities including rural electrification projects (RDSS scheme), but rural revenue is not separately disclosed as a percentage.

govt_capex.evidence: Significant portion of conductor and cable revenue linked to power sector capital expenditure (state DISCOMs, power transmission utilities). Exact government capex-linked % not disclosed without PDF.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Apar has working capital facilities (cash credit, bill discounting) that are floating rate. Exact % of total financial liabilities not confirmed without PDF.

crude_exposure.evidence: Apar's transformer oil segment (~25-30% of revenue historically) uses base oil derived from crude oil as primary raw material. Speciality oils division is heavily crude-linked. Exact consolidated RM % not confirmed without PDF.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Apar Industries uses a combination of natural hedges (USD raw material imports offset against USD export revenues) and forward contracts for residual exposure. The company has a board-approved hedging policy.
inr_exposure.evidence: Apar has significant export revenues (conductors, cables) priced in USD and also imports USD-denominated raw materials; net exposure hedged via forwards per past disclosures. Exact USD revenue % not confirmed without PDF.

pli_scheme.evidence: Apar Industries is in cables, conductors, and transformer oils. These sectors are not covered under current PLI schemes. No PLI beneficiary status in available disclosures.

govt_capex.evidence: Hitachi Energy India serves the Indian power sector predominantly — customers include power utilities (central and state), renewable energy developers, and industrial clients. The company's order book of Rs 19,245.9 crore at end-FY25 is heavily tied to India's government-driven T&D capex programmes. Specific government revenue percentage not disclosed in publicly accessible portions of the FY25 annual report.

inr_exposure.evidence: Export orders were ~22% of total orders in Q2FY25 and over 40% excluding a large one-time HVDC domestic order in certain quarters. Full-year revenue export split not disclosed in accessible public sources.

china_plus_one.evidence: NMDC has explicitly stated it has no plans to export iron ore to China. The government directed NMDC to focus on the domestic market. NMDC discontinued its long-term export agreements with Japan and Korea. As of FY25, NMDC is overwhelmingly domestic-focused with minimal to no exports.

govt_capex.evidence: NMDC is itself a Government of India (PSU) enterprise under the Ministry of Steel. Its customers are domestic steel producers including government-owned RINL and private mills (JSW Steel, Tata Steel, etc.). Revenue is not classified by government vs private capex in accessible public disclosures.

crude_exposure.evidence: NMDC is a mining company — key input costs are explosives, diesel/HSD for mining equipment and transport, and electricity. Crude oil (diesel) is an indirect input but specific percentage not publicly disclosed.

inr_exposure.evidence: NMDC sells iron ore in INR domestically. As of FY25, the company has stated it has no plans to export iron ore; exports are negligible. USD revenue exposure is minimal to none.

china_plus_one.evidence: Elgi Equipments has significant global export presence across North America, Europe, Australia, South East Asia, and Middle East, with ~46% of FY25 consolidated revenue from international markets. However, no explicit China+1 narrative with revenue attribution was found in accessible public sources for FY2024-25.

inr_exposure.evidence: Approximately 46% of FY25 consolidated revenue (~Rs 1,617 crore out of Rs 3,510 crore) was from international markets (North America, Europe, Australia, Middle East, South East Asia). A meaningful portion would be USD and EUR denominated. Specific hedging policy details not accessible in public sources.

rural.evidence: Radico Khaitan sells IMFL brands across urban, semi-urban and rural India. Regular/mass segment products (which constitute the majority of volumes) have significant rural and semi-urban distribution, but no explicit rural revenue percentage is disclosed in publicly available filings.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Company carries working capital borrowings which are typically floating rate, but exact split between fixed and floating rate debt is not publicly disclosed in summary form.

crude_exposure.evidence: Radico Khaitan is an alcobev company. Primary raw materials are Extra Neutral Alcohol (ENA), grains (maize, barley), glass bottles, and packaging. No significant crude oil exposure as a raw material.

inr_exposure.evidence: Export revenues estimated at ~5% of total revenues based on known export activity to Middle East, Africa, and select international markets. Exact hedging policy not retrievable without PDF access.

pli_scheme.evidence: Alcobev (IMFL) sector is not covered under any PLI scheme announced by the Government of India.

rural.evidence: CPCL is a petroleum refiner selling primarily to OMCs (Indian Oil, BPCL, HPCL) and institutional customers. It does not have direct rural retail exposure; end-consumer rural/urban split is not applicable or disclosed.

govt_capex.evidence: CPCL sells refined products to government OMCs (IOC being the parent), which could be considered government-linked revenue, but explicit govt capex exposure percentage is not disclosed.

rate_sensitive.evidence: CPCL carries significant working capital and term loan borrowings. As a PSU, much of its debt is from public sector banks and could be floating rate (linked to MCLR/repo). Exact split not accessible without PDF.

crude_exposure.evidence: Crude oil is the primary raw material for CPCL, constituting approximately 85-90% of total raw material and input costs, consistent with Indian refinery cost structures. CPCL processes approximately 10.5 MMTPA crude. GRM (Gross Refining Margin) is directly tied to crude differentials.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: CPCL primarily sells in INR to domestic OMCs. Crude oil purchases are USD-denominated, creating a natural USD payable exposure. The company typically uses forward contracts to hedge a portion of its forex payables as per RBI guidelines applicable to PSUs.
inr_exposure.evidence: As a domestic refiner, CPCL's revenues are predominantly in INR. USD exposure is primarily on the payables side (crude oil imports). Domestic product pricing is regulated/benchmarked to import parity pricing.

pli_scheme.evidence: Oil refining/petroleum sector is not a beneficiary of any PLI scheme announced by the Government of India.
